title: Venini (V.S.M. Venini & C. 1925–1932; Venini & C. from 1932)
motivation: Central 20th-century glasshouse: Martinuzzi, Buzzi, Scarpa, Bianconi, Wirkkala; nine Venini-related Le Stanze del Vetro exhibitions; Met, AIC holdings; catalogue raisonné exists.

title: V.S.M. Cappellin Venini & C. (1921–1925)
motivation: The partnership that started the modern 'soffiati' style under Zecchin; root of both Venini and M.V.M. Cappellin.

title: M.V.M. Cappellin & C. (1925–1931/32)
motivation: Where Carlo Scarpa began in glass; AIC holds 39 objects; 2018 catalogue raisonné; documented acid mark.

title: Barovier & Toso (with Artisti Barovier, Vetreria Artistica Barovier, S.A.I.A.R. Ferro Toso)
motivation: Longest documented family line on Murano; Ercole Barovier's innovations; lineage needs careful dating (conflicts 1883/84, 1890/96).

title: Seguso Vetri d'Arte (incl. Barovier Seguso & Ferro)
motivation: Poli's sommersi and Valve; Biennale presence 1930s–50s; founding date and name change disputed.

title: Vetreria Artistica Archimede Seguso
motivation: Archimede Seguso's own furnace from 1946; filigrana innovations (Merletti); Met holdings; 1991 Palazzo Ducale exhibition.

title: Salviati (Antonio Salviati and the Salviati firms)
motivation: Engine of the 19th-century revival; Met holds many objects; lineage between the 1859, 1866 and 1877 firms must be untangled before any website text.

title: Compagnia di Venezia e Murano / Pauly & C.
motivation: Murrine and historicist glass of the 1870s–80s (Met); later merged with Pauly & C.; founding dates disputed.

title: Fratelli Toso
motivation: Founded 1854; Ermanno Toso, Pollio Perelda, Rosanna Toso; 2024/25 Museo del Vetro exhibition.

title: Vetri Decorativi Rag. Aureliano Toso
motivation: Dino Martens' Oriente and Zanfirico pieces; Met holds an attributed vase; founding year inconsistent.

title: A.VE.M. – Arte Vetraria Muranese
motivation: Founded 1932 by maestri; Giulio Radi's metal-oxide experiments; Giorgio Ferro; Anzolo Fuga.

title: Gino Cenedese & C.
motivation: Barbini's corroso sculptures (1948 Biennale); later Antonio Da Ros; scholarly coverage still thin.

title: Vetreria Alfredo Barbini
motivation: Barbini's own furnace from 1950; family continuation (Flavio Barbini).

title: S.A.L.I.R. – Studio Ars et Labor Industrie Riunite
motivation: Leading Murano decorating/engraving workshop 1923–1993 (Balsamo Stella, Pelzel, Martens); Heiremans catalogue.

title: Vetreria Vistosi
motivation: Post-war design furnace (Pianon, Bianconi, Aulenti, Sottsass); continuity of the brand after the 1990s unclear.

title: Carlo Scarpa
motivation: Defining designer at M.V.M. Cappellin and Venini; DBI entry; two Le Stanze del Vetro catalogues; Met and AIC holdings.

title: Paolo Venini
motivation: Founder and designer; DBI entry with full chronology.

title: Vittorio Zecchin
motivation: First artistic director of the modern era (Cappellin Venini); DBI entry; LSV exhibition.

title: Napoleone Martinuzzi
motivation: Pulegoso; artistic director of V.S.M. Venini; museum director; DBI entry; LSV exhibition.

title: Ercole Barovier
motivation: Six decades of innovation at Barovier & Toso; DBI entry documents signature practice.

title: Archimede Seguso
motivation: Maestro and designer; key link between Barovier Seguso & Ferro and his own firm.

title: Flavio Poli
motivation: Artistic director of Seguso Vetri d'Arte 1934–1963; no DBI entry found – dossier depends on catalogues.

title: Dino Martens
motivation: Painter-designer of Aureliano Toso; career dates partly inconsistent in sources.

title: Fulvio Bianconi
motivation: Fazzoletto and Pezzati at Venini; LSV exhibition and catalogue raisonné.

title: Tomaso Buzzi
motivation: Short but decisive Venini period 1932–34; LSV catalogue raisonné.

title: Alfredo Barbini
motivation: Maestro whose career runs through four firms before his own; explicitly requested case.

title: Giulio Radi
motivation: A.VE.M. co-founder and artistic director; metal-oxide experiments.

title: Antonio (Nini) Da Ros
motivation: Cenedese artistic director (explicitly requested case); only Tier C sources and one museum attribution so far.

title: Angelo Barovier (15th century)
motivation: Cristallo attributed to him; anchors the historical introduction; homonym of Angelo Barovier (b. 1927).

title: Lino Tagliapietra
motivation: Bridge from Murano maestro tradition to the international studio-glass movement; Met holdings.
